#5509. U.S. crude falls over 2% as Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia rattle traders

Free daily briefing on global business news.

WTI fell 2.19% to $101 and Brent fell 1.89% to $114.51 as traders weighed supply risks against demand worries

U.S. crude oil futures dropped by more than 2% on Monday, with traders balancing the possibility of additional Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia against worries that steep prices could dent demand.

West Texas Intermediate futures lost 2.19% and changed hands at $101 per barrel. Brent crude futures gave up 1.89%, leaving them at $114.51. The pullback followed a rally on Friday, when prices settled close to $3 higher after Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. Over the course of last week, Brent gained 6% while WTI rose 2.3%.

The Houthis claimed responsibility for Saturday strikes on the principal airport in Riyadh and on Saudi oil installations. Saudi Arabia stated Sunday that it had shot down further missiles and drones. The kingdom brought part of the airport's operations back online Sunday even though earlier attacks had left it damaged, according to CNBC. The Houthis threatened more strikes.

Hopes of easing tensions between the U.S. and Iran also weighed on prices. Qatari mediators traveled to Tehran on Sunday to help calm tensions across the region, working in concert with the U.S., according to Reuters.

“Concerns over renewed military hostilities in the Middle East, which drove much of last week’s crude rally, have eased this morning, but the reprieve may prove temporary,” said Vandana Hari, founder of Vanda Insights, according to Reuters.

Michael Alfaro, chief investment officer at Gallo Partners, told CNBC that geopolitical uncertainty has inflated oil prices by about $20 per barrel. He said a serious hit to Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, or to additional refineries, could push prices up, though any further rise might eat into consumption.

"What we would likely see if oil pushed above 120, 130, 140 dollars a barrel for Brent, that is, you're going to see more demand destruction," Alfaro said, according to CNBC. He added that harm to refining capacity could grow into a structural problem that lingers through 2027 and later years.

Saudi Arabia shut down its East-West Pipeline after drone attacks from Iraq in September. The pipeline can move up to 7 million barrels per day and had served as an export route that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz. Brent climbed above $108 a barrel at the time as traders worried about when the pipeline would reopen.

Domestically, the Energy Department on Friday approved the release of as many as 400,000 barrels from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, aimed at easing a supply disruption at a Louisiana refinery, according to CNBC.

Energy ministers from Saudi Arabia and Singapore announced on Monday that state-owned Saudi Aramco will begin holding crude in Singapore storage during the latter half of 2027.

#5508. Is the Crypto Market Walking Into a Bull Trap? Bitcoin ETF Records Five Straight Days of Outflow

The CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

Bitcoin’s latest recovery attempt is running into a serious problem: institutional investors are pulling money out of the market. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF recorded five consecutive days of net outflows, shedding $1.44 billion between November 5 and November 11.

Bitcoin is now trading near $73,500, struggling to reclaim the $75,000 level. Bitcoin ETF outflow streak raises a bigger question: Is the crypto market walking into another bull trap?

The timing is particularly concerning. Bitcoin briefly reclaimed $80,000 on November 4 before reversing sharply the following day. Crypto has since struggled to regain momentum, leaving us questioning buyers’ decisions and whether we are stepping in too early.

The latest Bitcoin ETF withdrawals included $430.2 million on November 5, followed by another $411.9 million on November 6. Outflows continued on November 9, 10, and 11.

BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for most of the selling pressure. The fund alone recorded $269.7 million in net outflows yesterday.

The latest Bitcoin ETF outflow streak shows that institutional demand is struggling to support the market’s recovery. Five consecutive sessions of withdrawals have removed $1.44 billion from U.S. spot Bitcoin funds. BlackRock’s IBIT accounted for three-quarters of that amount.

However, institutional demand has not disappeared entirely. Morgan Stanley’s Bitcoin ETF attracted $9 million yesterday, offering a small counterpoint to the ETF-wide selling.

Glassnode’s latest Week 46 report adds another warning. Bitcoin has fallen below the short-term holder cost basis of $75,600. This leaves recent buyers sitting on unrealized losses.

The research firm also points to shrinking stablecoin supply and continued ETF selling. Both developments display that fresh capital is struggling to enter the market.

This creates an uncomfortable setup for anyone buying the latest dip. A short-lived recovery could attract retail investors before another wave of selling pushes prices lower.

Bitcoin’s derivatives market offers another piece of the puzzle. BTC futures open interest remains above $50 billion, while funding rates remain positive. This number somehow paints a clear picture: leveraged traders are still paying to maintain bullish positions.

However, leverage has already started coming out of the market. Open interest has declined, and much of the long-side leverage near current prices has been flushed.

That creates two possible outcomes. If spot demand returns, reduced leverage could help Bitcoin recover without triggering another major liquidation cascade. Alternatively, another failed breakout could leave remaining leveraged buyers exposed to further downside.

For now, $75,600 is the important recovery threshold. Reclaiming that level would put Bitcoin back above the short-term holder cost basis and improve market sentiment.

A grinding climb toward $80,000 would offer stronger evidence that buyers are regaining control, but losing the $72,000 area could expose BTC to another test of $70,000.

The bull trap argument also has a counterpoint. There is accumulation among two large wallet cohorts, while selling momentum has started weakening. This shows that some investors are already positioning for a recovery.

The market does not need another dramatic crash to trap investors. Sometimes, all it takes is a convincing bounce that runs out of buyers.

#5506. Saudi Arabia told OPEC its oil output hit a wartime high in October

Free daily briefing on global business news.

Production rose from 8.372 million barrels a day in September as Brent futures fell about 21% so far in November to $93

Andrey Rudakov / Bloomberg via Getty Images

Saudi Arabia told OPEC it pumped 10.563 million barrels a day of crude in October, a rise from September's 8.372 million.

That was a 26% increase and the highest level since before the war began, according to Bloomberg. Saudi Arabia told OPEC it produced 10.882 million barrels a day in February, the final month before the Iran war upended Middle East supply, according to Reuters.

The Saudi rebound is spearheading a wider pickup in production across the region, which is easing prices, according to Bloomberg. Brent futures have dropped about 18% since the start of the month, leaving them at $93 a barrel.

Saudi Arabia's reported figure sits above its OPEC quota, according to Bloomberg. OPEC measures compliance with figures drawn from third-party estimates instead of the numbers members submit themselves. Those secondary sources put Saudi output at 9.194 million barrels a day in October, OPEC said.

OPEC+ producers pumped 41.23 million barrels a day in October, up 2.04 million from September, according to secondary sources cited by OPEC. Iraq told OPEC it produced 4.888 million barrels a day, which Bloomberg described as a new wartime high for the country.

Saudi Arabia has run covert shuttle voyages with its tankers via the Strait of Hormuz, copying an approach the United Arab Emirates first used earlier in the war, according to Bloomberg. The kingdom has additionally leaned on a second pipeline to the Red Sea, which has been attacked.

Speaking at an Abu Dhabi industry event last week, Saudi Aramco CEO Amin Nasser said the company intends to "maximize production going forward in the fourth quarter," according to Bloomberg.

The output increase comes as OPEC and its allies examine the volumes each member can technically produce as groundwork for 2027 output targets. The review is expected to wrap up within the next few days, according to Bloomberg. When the full OPEC+ group convenes online on Nov. 29 to talk over 2027 targets, it will draw on that assessment.

The U.S.-Israeli war on Iran has held Gulf OPEC+ producers far below their output ceilings in recent months. Brent traded around $73 a barrel before the conflict began in late February.

#5504. Kalshi and Polymarket claim 98% accuracy in calling midterm races

Free daily briefing on global business news.

A New York Times analysis found prediction markets did no better than election forecasts for most of the race

Kalshi said the candidates its traders favored won 98% of resolved races in Tuesday's midterm elections. The company announced the figure on Wednesday.

The tally covers 479 of 487 races resolved as of 6 a.m. ET on Nov. 4, Kalshi said. Favorites won 356 of 360 House races, 32 of 33 Senate races and 33 of 34 governor races.

Polymarket said that, judged against the day before the election, 98.4% of its settled contests had pointed to the correct winner, according to The Associated Press. Polymarket put its hit rate at roughly 97% for the Senate and gubernatorial contests and at 98.6% for those in the House.

Kalshi said its markets for House control passed 99% likelihood at 8:10 p.m. ET and its Senate control markets passed 99% at 9 p.m. ET, hours ahead of the networks. Trading volume on its 2026 midterm markets topped $2.5 billion, compared with $1.3 billion for the 2024 cycle, the company said.

In a separate analysis, Kalshi said directional accuracy for races called by 6:26 a.m. ET on Nov. 4 rose from 93.8% three months out to 98.2% when polls closed. Brier scores, on which lower is better, fell from 0.040 to 0.016, the company said.

Outside experts urged caution. Ross Dahlke, a University of Wisconsin-Madison professor, said the figures include only resolved markets, which may be easier to predict, and that many races were fairly certain going into Election Day, according to The Associated Press.

An analysis by The New York Times found that prediction markets fared about the same as election forecasts through most of the midterm campaign. Markets gained an edge in the closing days, the Times said, once polls and forecasts had gone out of date. Kalshi told the Times that its ability to post odds on par with seasoned forecasters well ahead of voting demonstrated the markets’ forecasting strength.

Polymarket did not respond to a request for comment from The New York Times.

Koleman Strumpf, an economics professor at Wake Forest University who studies prediction markets, gave the markets a B, according to Bloomberg. He said the markets pointed the right way but underestimated how large the Democratic wave would be.

Kalshi said on X $TWTR that its markets outperformed forecasting models including those of Silver Bulletin, FiftyPlusOne and The Economist, according to Bloomberg. Nate Silver, who runs Silver Bulletin, said his model and others showed the Democratic wave sooner and more aggressively.

#5503. Agent fleets drag the messaging layer from afterthought to AI’s coordination core

Data center telemetry, sandboxed AI workloads and fleets of agents are pushing more machine-to-machine traffic through infrastructure than ever before, exposing the limits of messaging systems built for steadier demand.

That shift is drawing attention to the Neural Autonomic Transport System, an open-source messaging system that lets applications and services exchange messages by topic. Created in 2010, NATS graduated from the Cloud Native Computing Foundation in November 2026. Its simple design suits AI workloads, according to Andrew Connolly (pictured, left), NATS project maintainer at Synadia Communications Inc., a provider of managed NATS services. When AI tools like Lovable can turn a plain-language prompt into a working web app, the messaging layer has to keep updates flowing as sandboxes come and go.

“What’s changed in the current context, or landscape, is everything is really ephemeral. If you take the Lovable example, connections coming and going really fast, tons of churn, tons of sandboxes, all these things spinning up, spinning down,” Connolly said. “Not every technology can handle that.”

Connolly and Waldemar Quevedo (right), project maintainer of NATS at Synadia, spoke with theCUBE’s John Furrier and Rebecca Knight at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how NATS handles traffic from short-lived sandboxes, carries data center telemetry and helps AI agents hand off work. (* Disclosure below.)

The demands go well beyond app sandboxes. The project itself has grown from single-cluster deployments into a system that spans data centers, regions and clouds, with one AI app builder recently rebuilding its real-time service on NATS to serve millions of subscriptions, Quevedo noted.

“NATS has evolved to be able to communicate multiple data centers with a super cluster topology with the gateways,” Quevedo said. “It is smart [at routing] the interest graph out to multiple regions, multiple availability zones, multi-cloud.”

Some data center operators use NATS to carry power and cooling telemetry, and Nvidia Corp. built its AI factory event bus on the system as part of its DSX reference architecture, Connolly said. NATS can also route messages across fleets of AI agents, with its JetStream persistence engine and key-value store preserving the state agents need to hand off work.

“In some sense, agentic systems are just microservices systems, but at a bigger scale,” Connolly said. “NATS was good for microservices. It’s going to be great for AI agents.”

#5502. Microsoft 365 Outage: CIOs Should Verify Recovery Across Workflows and Security Controls, Says Infotech

The Microsoft 365 outage has shown how email dependencies can interrupt business processes even when other functions remain available. Infotech's research note, Microsoft 365 Outage: Immediate Actions for CIOs, covers recovery validation, potential security coverage gaps, and continuity measures for prolonged cloud outages.

ARLINGTON, Va., Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- In response to the Microsoft 365 outage that began on November 12, Infotech, a global research and API-driven advisory firm, is recommending that CIOs verify the recovery of business-critical workflows, integrations, and security controls before declaring normal operations restored. The firm's new research note, Microsoft 365 Outage: Immediate Actions for CIOs, also advises organizations to document service disruptions and preserve evidence for potential service level agreement claims.

The outage began Thursday afternoon with Exchange Online mailbox access failures in the Americas and affected functions in Teams, SharePoint, Copilot, and Defender. Thursday night, servers that had returned to service failed again under load, and Microsoft added capacity and began rolling back a recent network change. According to the note's midday ET update on November 13, availability was improving, but intermittent issues persisted, and Microsoft had not given a restoration time. At that point, Microsoft had reported no evidence of malicious activity, and the root cause was still under investigation.

"CIOs need a clear basis for telling the business it can return to normal operations," says Kate Wood, AVP of Research Development at Infotech. "That means knowing which critical processes have been tested, where security coverage still needs checking, and which teams must continue using workarounds. Executive updates should make those outstanding issues visible so that business teams can plan their next steps."

The examples summarized in Infotech's note show contingency plans holding where a manual route existed and stalling where email was the only channel. According to news reports, disruptions included delays to patient referrals and court communications, while some organizations maintained critical operations using other systems or manual procedures. Core Teams messaging and meetings and direct SharePoint file access also remained largely operational, reinforcing the need to assess the specific functions and dependencies supporting each business process.

Recommended Actions for Microsoft 365 Response and RecoveryInfotech advises CIOs to focus on maintaining operations and documenting impacts. IT teams should log unresolved issues and failed workarounds throughout recovery, giving executives a clear view of operating status and creating a record to guide improvements to continuity plans.

The firm's Microsoft 365 Outage: Immediate Actions for CIOs research note groups its recommendations as follows:

For longer-term readiness, Infotech emphasizes testing continuity procedures against prolonged outages affecting multiple cloud services. Organizations should identify where reliance on a single cloud environment creates shared points of failure and establish independent continuity options where the business impact justifies them.

Additional resources include the firm's Develop a Business Continuity Plan, Create a Right-Sized Disaster Recovery Plan, and IT Communications Research Center.

#5501. Suspected cyberattack hit supermarket freezers across Europe in second wave

Free daily briefing on global business news.

Retailers in Belgium, Luxembourg, Sweden, Estonia and Ireland reported temperature spikes; no one has claimed responsibility

Ahold Delhaize said an IT incident caused temperatures to climb in refrigeration systems across dozens of supermarkets it runs in Belgium and Luxembourg on Monday, according to The Guardian. Grocers in Sweden, Estonia and Ireland reported similar problems, making this the second suspected cyberattack on European store cooling systems after one in France.

Ahold Delhaize spokesperson Sarah De Meester said the company is investigating the temperature increases, according to The Guardian. Stephan Moelans, CEO of refrigeration firm Sabcobel, said the attack switched the units' evaporators to defrost mode, according to Al Jazeera. Moelans said technicians were called out starting at 1 a.m. to cut the compromised installations off from the grid, according to The Guardian.

A Colruyt Group spokesperson said the refrigeration equipment in five Spar shops was targeted, according to Reuters. Colruyt franchises out the Spar outlets it oversees across Belgium.

In Sweden, Coop said six stores were affected, and ICA said a small number of its outlets had their cooling and freezing equipment knocked offline by an incident, according to The Guardian. Axfood said hackers broke into freezers at a Gothenburg-area hub that handles home-delivery orders, according to Al Jazeera.

John Billow, head of Sweden’s national cybersecurity center, said the agency is handling several incidents tied to cooling equipment in stores, according to Al Jazeera. He said Sweden has many exposed operational technology devices that need updates or patches.

Jann Mutso, CEO of technology supplier Kitman Coldtech, said at least one Estonian grocery chain was hit and that its temperatures had been pushed up to 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit), according to Al Jazeera. Ireland’s SuperValu said a “cyber incident” compromised one particular type of refrigeration unit in 13 of the chain’s 223 stores, according to Al Jazeera.

No one has claimed responsibility for Monday's incidents or the French attack, according to Al Jazeera.

The incidents follow an October attack in France that disabled refrigeration at Intermarché, Coopérative U and Leclerc stores and drove temperatures in refrigerators and freezers up to 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit) through a continuous defrost cycle. French police said hackers took over the cooling equipment of as many as 700 supermarkets, according to The Guardian. The hackers took over control units that came largely from Danfoss, a Danish company.

Ahold Delhaize notified Dutch police last month of a cybersecurity incident, according to The Guardian.

#5499. Oil prices fall more than 4% as Iran peace talks ease supply fears

Free daily briefing on global business news.

Brent crude for January delivery fell 4.2% to $108.68 a barrel, reversing some of last week's gains ahead of Tuesday's U.S. midterm elections

Oil prices tumbled by upwards of 4% Monday, with negotiations to bring the U.S.-Iran conflict to a close soothing worries about Middle East supply.

Brent crude futures expiring in January slid 4.2% to $108.68 per barrel. U.S. West Texas Intermediate contracts due in December declined 4.3% to $99.61, while the January contracts shed 4.2% to reach $97.90.

The declines wiped out part of the previous week's rally. Brent had closed out October at a six-month peak.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Sunday that negotiations with mediators from Qatar about reopening the Strait of Hormuz were still under way, though no deal had been reached. He added that Iran had sent a delegation headed by a deputy foreign minister to Qatar, while no face-to-face meeting with U.S. officials was on the schedule.

Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade, described the move as a technical pullback after last week’s strong gains, according to Reuters. He cited continued optimism about a diplomatic breakthrough, along with a weekend that passed without significant fighting escalating.

The risk of renewed fighting remains. According to The Wall Street Journal, the U.S. has instructed a number of Gulf Arab states to get ready for a possible brief but intense military operation against Iran once Tuesday's midterm elections are over. President Donald Trump has yet to reach a conclusive decision about resuming strikes.

Seven OPEC+ producers decided Sunday to leave their targets for December output as they were. The group, whose members include Saudi Arabia and Russia, will next convene on Nov. 29 to assess output for January.

Regional attacks also continued over the weekend. The Saudi-led coalition announced Sunday an operation against assets that the Iran-backed Houthi militants in Yemen depend on for their drone and missile efforts.

Vice President JD Vance wrote last week to Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, to try to revive peace talks. Trump said he had approved the outreach, which was meant to outline a possible structure for talks rather than present a full peace plan.

Qatari mediators also offered a new plan to end the fighting among Iran, the U.S. and Israel. A high-ranking Iranian official dismissed the offer as unacceptable. The U.S. and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding on June 17, but the agreement collapsed.

#5498. Exchange Ledgers in the Middle as CFTC and SEC Diverge on What “Delivery” Means

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

A customer buys a token on a U.S. exchange and the app shows the balance. Under the CFTC's December 14 framework, nothing has been delivered yet.

Under the SEC's crypto proposal, delivery doesn't decide the question at all. An October 27 comment letter asks the two agencies to settle on one answer.

Open almost any crypto exchange app after a purchase and you'll see a clean number: 1.0000 ETH, available. To the customer, the asset is theirs. To the exchange's database, it's a row in an internal ledger. To federal regulators, that row is now being judged by two different tests that don't agree on what it means.

The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has opened an advance notice of proposed rulemaking on what it calls Regulation Crypto Asset Transactions (CTX) and Regulation Crypto Asset Markets (CAM). It sets out the agency's first formal view of "actual delivery" for crypto since it withdrew its 2020 guidance last December. Comments close on December 14.

The Securities and Exchange Commission's Regulation Crypto Assets proposal takes a different view of the same moment. Then, on October 27, a comment letter on the SEC's file raised the gap directly. It described the situation as "two conflicting definitions of the same physical facts" and asked the agencies to "please coordinate the definitions."

Delivery matters because it decides which rulebook applies.

For the CFTC, the answer comes from Section 2(c)(2)(D) of the Commodity Exchange Act. A leveraged, margined or financed retail commodity trade is treated like a futures contract unless "actual delivery" happens within 28 days. If delivery happens in time, the trade falls outside futures rules. If it doesn't, the exchange is effectively running a futures venue.

For the SEC, the question is whether a token is still part of an investment contract. Under the August proposal, a covered investment contract ends when the issuer has finished or permanently stopped its essential managerial efforts and files a Form TR transition report. Whether the buyer has received the token is not part of that test.

So one agency treats delivery as the deciding question, and the other barely considers it.

The CFTC's position is still preliminary, but it is detailed. Published in the Federal Register on October 13, the notice relies on the Monex case standard: actual delivery requires "the transfer of some meaningful degree of possession or control."

For crypto, the agency suggests that possession and control "may require possession of the credentials (e.g., private key(s))." It takes three positions that matter most to exchanges:

The agency is also asking whether control has to be exclusive, whether delivery can happen while a lien or security interest is outstanding, and how financing offered in an exchange's standard account documents affects whether a trade is covered at all.

The SEC's proposal, released on August 18, deals with a different question. It creates offering exemptions, including a $5 million startup exemption over four years, and a safe harbor for when a crypto asset's investment contract ends. Neither depends on where the token sits.

Under the proposal, a token held in a customer's self-custody wallet and a token recorded on an exchange's books are treated the same way. In both cases, the investment contract question depends on the issuer's managerial efforts and its filings.

That is the gap the October 27 letter tries to close. Its author, who describes themselves as a fintech founder designing a consumer platform, argues that "where the customer holds the private keys or execution is on-chain, with custody evidence, the asset should be treated as delivered and the covered-investment-contract analysis should end there."

Running four common exchange transactions through both frameworks shows where the tests split.

Trade one: a fully paid purchase left on the exchange.

Trade two: the same purchase withdrawn to a self-custody wallet on day three.

Trade three: a margined purchase kept on the exchange's ledger for 30 days.

Trade four: an on-chain swap that settles directly into the user's wallet.

The pattern is consistent. Self-custody is the only position that clearly counts as delivery under the CFTC's view and also ends the analysis under the letter's proposed SEC fix. Everything left on an exchange's internal ledger stays in an unclear position. The CFTC treats it as undelivered and the SEC's text doesn't address it.

The letter was filed on October 27, a week after the SEC's October 20 comment deadline. It is anonymous and brief, but its main concern is practical. If the definitions stay separate, it warns, founders will have to design products around whichever rule is stricter.

It is the only filing on either docket so far that sets the two definitions side by side.

The CFTC process is still at the advance-notice stage, so a formal proposal will follow. For U.S. platforms, though, the direction is clear. Under the CFTC's preliminary reading, an exchange that keeps customer assets in internal ledger accounts has not delivered them. If that exchange also offers margin or financing, it is on track to be treated as a futures venue.

The SEC's final rule could adopt the letter's custody-based approach or keep delivery out of its analysis entirely. Until one of those happens, the same ledger entry can be undelivered for one regulator and irrelevant for the other.

Exchanges and their customers have until December 14 to say which definition should prevail. The real decision is whether "delivered" ends up meaning the same thing at both agencies.

#5497. Fly-E Group, Inc. Announces Second Quarter and First Half of Fiscal Year 2027 Financial Results

NEW YORK, Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly-E Group, Inc. (Nasdaq: FLYE) ("Fly-E" or the "Company"), an electric vehicle company engaged in designing, installing, selling, and renting smart electric motorcycles, electric bikes, and electric scooters, today announced its unaudited financial results for the second quarter and first half of fiscal year 2027 ended September 30, 2026.

Second quarter of Fiscal Year 2027 Financial Summary

Mr. Zhou (Andy) Ou, Chief Executive Officer of Fly-E, commented, "During the second quarter, our operational network stabilized following the retail restructuring, with our top-line revenue holding steady sequentially. Our wholesale revenues grew 21.4% year-over-year and accounted for a significantly higher proportion of our total revenue. This evolving revenue mix, combined with promotional pricing in our retail business, naturally influenced our overall margin profile for the period. Meanwhile, we continued to control store-level costs and address corporate matters carefully to strengthen the Company's foundation for the future. By maintaining our operational network and disciplined cost management, we are dedicated to preserving business stability while positioning Fly-E to explore strategic opportunities for long-term growth."

Second quarter of Fiscal Year 2027 Financial Results

Net revenues were $2.6 million in the second quarter of fiscal year 2027, a decrease of 33.7% from $3.9 million in the same period last year. The decrease was primarily driven by a lower sales volume of 7,392 units in the second quarter of fiscal year 2027, compared to 18,564 in the same period last year, resulting from the reduction in our direct retail store count to four stores as of September 30, 2026, compared to 11 stores as of September 30, 2025.

Cost of revenues was $2.4 million in the second quarter of fiscal year 2027, a decrease of 18.8% from $2.9 million in the same period last year, primarily aligning with lower sales volume driven by the downsizing of our retail store network.

Gross profit was $0.2 million in the second quarter of fiscal year 2027, compared to $1.0 million in the same period last year. Gross margin was 8.1% in the second quarter of fiscal year 2027, compared to 25.0% in the same period last year. The decrease in gross margin was primarily attributable to a structural mix shift from direct retail toward lower-priced wholesale channels, further impacted by competitive retail pricing and inventory clearance discounts.

Total operating expenses were $1.8 million in the second quarter of fiscal year 2027, a decrease of 9.8% compared to $2.0 million in the same period last year. The decrease was primarily attributable to store-level operational savings, which were partially offset by increases in expected credit losses and professional fees.

Net loss was $1.7 million in the second quarter of fiscal year 2027, compared to $1.8 million in the same period last year.

Basic and Diluted Earnings (Losses) per Share

Basic and diluted losses per share were $1.07 in the second quarter of fiscal year 2027, compared to $2.18 in the same period last year.

EBITDA was negative $1.3 million in the second quarter of fiscal year 2027, compared to negative EBITDA of $1.0 million in the same period last year.

First Half of Fiscal Year 2027 Financial Results

Net revenues were $5.3 million in the first half of fiscal year 2027, a decrease of 42.2% from $9.2 million in the same period last year. The decrease was primarily driven by a significant reduction in direct retail store counts, resulting in a lower sales volume of 14,950 units in the first half of fiscal year 2027, compared to 29,012 in the same period last year.

Cost of revenues was $4.8 million in the first half of fiscal year 2027, a decrease of 19.5% from $6.0 million in the same period last year, primarily reflecting lower sales volume following the downsizing of our retail store network.

Gross profit was $0.5 million in the first half of fiscal year 2027, compared to $3.2 million in the same period last year. Gross margin was 9.5% in the first half of fiscal year 2027, compared to 35.1% in the same period last year. The decrease in gross margin was primarily attributable to the greater revenue percentage of wholesale channels at lower-priced wholesale pricing, as well as promotional retail pricing adjustment and inventory clearance discounts.

Total operating expenses were $5.7 million in the first half of fiscal year 2027, a decrease of 2.2% compared to $5.8 million in the same period last year. The decrease was primarily attributable to operational cost savings from retail store reductions, which were offset by increases in expected credit losses and software development fees.

Net loss was $5.6 million in the first half of fiscal year 2027, compared to $3.8 million in the same period last year.

Basic and Diluted Earnings (Losses) per Share

Basic and diluted losses per share were $3.48 in the first half of fiscal year 2027, compared to $6.58 in the same period last year.

EBITDA was negative $4.7 million in the first half of fiscal year 2027, compared to negative EBITDA of $2.2 million in the same period last year.

As of September 30, 2026, the Company had cash of $0.5 million, compared to $0.3 million as of March 31, 2026.

Fly-E Group, Inc. is an electric vehicle company that is principally engaged in designing, installing, selling, and renting smart electric motorcycles, electric bikes, and electric scooters under the brand "Fly E-Bike." The Company's commitment is to encourage people to incorporate eco-friendly transportation into their active lifestyles, ultimately contributing towards building a more environmentally friendly future. For more information, please visit the Company's website: https://investors.flyebike.com.

To supplement our financial information presented in accordance with the generally accepted accounting principles in the United States (the "U.S. GAAP"), management periodically uses certain "non-GAAP financial measures," as such term is defined under the rules of the SEC, to clarify and enhance understanding of past performance and prospects for the future. Generally, a non-GAAP financial measure is a numerical measure of a company's operating performance, financial position or cash flows that excludes or includes amounts that are included in or excluded from the most directly comparable measure calculated and presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP. For example, non-GAAP measures may exclude the impact of certain items such as acquisitions, divestitures, gains, losses and impairments, or items outside of management's control. Management believes that the following non-GAAP financial measure provides investors and analysts useful insight into our financial position and operating performance. Any non-GAAP measure provided should be viewed in addition to, and not as an alternative to, the most directly comparable measure determined in accordance with U.S. GAAP. Further, the calculation of these non-GAAP financial measures may differ from the calculation of similarly titled financial measures presented by other companies and therefore may not be comparable among companies.

We use EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization) to evaluate our operating performance. We believe EBITDA provides additional insight into our underlying, ongoing operating performance and facilitates year-to-year comparisons by excluding the earnings impact of interest, tax, depreciation and amortization and that presenting EBITDA is more representative of our operational performance and may be more useful for investors.

We reconcile our non-GAAP financial measure to our net income, which is our most directly comparable financial measure calculated and presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP. EBITDA includes adjustments for provision for income taxes, as applicable, interest income and expense, depreciation, and amortization. EBITDA does not represent and should not be considered an alternative to net income as determined by U.S. GAAP, and our calculations thereof may not be comparable to those reported by other companies. We believe EBITDA is an important measure of operating performance and provides useful information to investors because it highlights trends in our business that may not otherwise be apparent when relying solely on U.S. GAAP measures and because it eliminates items that have less bearing on our operating performance. EBITDA, as presented herein, is a supplemental measure of our performance that is not required by, or presented in accordance with, U.S. GAAP. We use non-GAAP financial measures as supplements to our U.S. GAAP results in order to provide a more complete understanding of the factors and trends affecting our business. EBITDA is a measure of operating performance that is not defined by U.S. GAAP and should not be considered a substitute for net (loss) income as determined in accordance with U.S. GAAP.

#5496. Mirendil raises $1B in funding to speed up AI model development

Mirendil Inc., a provider of software that speeds up artificial intelligence development, has raised $1 billion in early-stage funding.

The startup stated on Thursday that Kleiner Perkins and Clearlake Capital jointly led the Series A investment. They were joined by more than a half-dozen others including Google LLC.

Mirendil was launched last year by two former Google DeepMind and Anthropic PBC researchers. Chief Executive Officer Behnam Neyshabur is a co-inventor of SAM, a popular algorithm that makes AI models better at tasks they were not specifically trained to perform. Chief Technology Officer Harsh Mehta, in turn, spent his time at Google DeepMind and Anthropic working on pretraining projects. Pretraining is a term for the initial phase of the AI development workflow.

Mirendil’s first product, Lor, is a platform that automates many of the tasks involved in model training runs. The company says that the software does so by splitting work among hundreds of AI agents.

Large language model development involves a significant amount of trial and error. Researchers create multiple versions of an algorithm that differ from one another in small ways and compare them to find the most performant variant. According to Mirendil, Lor can automate that workflow. If an error crops up during the evaluation, the platform fixes it automatically.

Earlier this year, Mirendil asked one of its researchers to build a coding model that can compete with leading open-source LLMs. Usually, such projects are carried out by teams of specialists. Mirendil says that its automation technology enabled the researcher to build the model without any help from colleagues. The project cost $10 million and took about 3.5 months to complete.

The company’s agents wrote more than 99% of the code that powers the model, which is called Mirendil-Base. They set up infrastructure, found a suitable training algorithm and collected training data from the web. The agents then refined both the training dataset and Mirendil-Base’s architecture to boost output quality.

The LLM is the foundation of a specialized coding model called Fern that the company unveiled last month. According to Mirendil, it’s designed to automate programming challenges commonly encountered by AI labs. Fern can process 10 million input tokens per prompt, or 10 times more than Claude Opus 5.5. That’s the equivalent of about a half-million lines of code.

Fern is based on a version of Mirendil-Base with 100 billion to 500 billion parameters. Late last month, the company previewed two upgraded versions of the latter model with between 500 billion and 10 trillion parameters. Mirendil plans to use those algorithms to develop more capable LLMs.

#5495. JetBlue creditors are hiring restructuring advisers as bonds crash to 42 cents

Free daily briefing on global business news.

JetBlue's $2 billion of notes due 2031 traded near 80 cents on the dollar this month; its stock has fallen more than half since August

JetBlue Airways has a group of senior creditors engaged with PJT Partners, a restructuring adviser, and the law firm Akin, as the airline deals with heavy cash outflows and high oil prices, according to The Wall Street Journal.

The airline's $2 billion of notes due 2031 sank to 42 cents on the dollar on Thursday and traded in the mid-40s on Friday, according to The Wall Street Journal, which cited market participants and Finra data. The decline followed a recent bondholder call. Finra data shows the notes changed hands at roughly 80 cents per dollar of face value earlier in October.

JetBlue stock closed at $2.62 on Friday, down 0.94%, and has fallen 42% this year. It has lost more than half its value since the start of August.

"JetBlue remains confident in its JetForward strategy and the progress being made toward returning to sustained profitability," the company said in an emailed statement, according to Reuters. A JetBlue representative told The Wall Street Journal that management's focus is on boosting revenue and developing a business that earns more. JetBlue plans to give an account of how it is progressing and where its finances are headed when it hosts its call on third-quarter results on Tuesday.

Creditors bring in advisers once they fear a borrower may not return their money in full or on time, according to The Wall Street Journal. Spirit Airlines shut down operations this year after repeated bankruptcy filings, and investors holding airline debt have been wary ever since, the Journal said.

JetBlue held $1.66 billion of cash, plus cash equivalents, as of June 30, set against $8.5 billion of borrowings and finance lease commitments, according to its filings. Much of that debt is secured by JetBlue's aircraft fleet and its TrueBlue loyalty program, according to The Wall Street Journal. Close to two-thirds of the company's assets, spanning property, equipment and intangibles, have been put up as security for lenders, according to its quarterly filings.

Some market participants fear that piling on more debt could leave JetBlue little room to maneuver if a turnaround fails, according to The Wall Street Journal. The airline also faces possible pressure from credit-card processors, which may demand that carriers hold back collateral should conditions deteriorate, the Journal said. JetBlue said it was under no such obligation when June ended.

Higher jet fuel costs tied to the Iran war have squeezed margins at U.S. airlines even as fares rose and travelers kept flying at a consistent pace, according to Reuters.

JetBlue reported a first-quarter net loss of $319 million in April, wider than the $208 million loss a year earlier. Jet fuel cost 15.2% more per gallon than in the same period a year before, and the company ended the quarter with $2.4 billion in liquidity. JetBlue arranged $500 million of financing secured by aircraft in April, and the full amount had been tapped by June 30, according to The Wall Street Journal.

#5493. Christine Lagarde is resigning as head of the European Central Bank months early

Free daily briefing on global business news.

The departure gives European leaders time to settle on a replacement before France holds its presidential vote in 2027

European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde will step down on Feb. 7, 2027, ahead of the scheduled end of her term.

Lagarde informed the ECB's Governing Council and European Council President António Costa of the decision on Thursday, the ECB said. The European Council will appoint her successor following the nomination process outlined in Article 283 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, the ECB said. The Governing Council gave her a long standing ovation, the ECB said.

Her eight-year term had been set to expire on Oct. 31, 2027, according to The Associated Press.

In a clip she shared on X $TWTR, Lagarde called it "a great pride and a huge privilege to serve this institution."

Costa said the selection process "will be initiated today and will proceed without delay."

The departure gives European leaders time to settle on a replacement before France holds its presidential vote in 2027. Two other top ECB posts are also changing hands. Chief economist Philip Lane's term ends May 31, and executive board member Isabel Schnabel is leaving Jan. 3 to join the International Monetary Fund, according to The Associated Press.

Leaders are expected to strike a package deal that spreads the three open jobs across E.U. member states, according to The Associated Press.

Klaas Knot, who used to head the Netherlands' central bank, and Pablo Hernandez de Cos, a onetime Spanish central bank governor, are regarded as the leading contenders to take over from Lagarde, according to Reuters.

Lagarde’s announcement landed on the same day the ECB is scheduled to publish its interest rate decision at 1:15 p.m. GMT (9:15 a.m. ET), with her regular press conference set for 1:45 p.m. GMT, according to Reuters. The bank is broadly predicted to leave borrowing costs unchanged, with the deposit rate staying at 2.5%, according to Reuters.

#5492. RYAN KAVANAUGH TO RECEIVE OUTSTANDING VIRTUAL PRODUCTION AWARD AT INFINITY FESTIVAL'S 2026 MONOLITH AWARDS FOR ACME STUDIOS WORK

Two-Day Showcase Expands Lineup with ACME's Ryan Kavanaugh alongside George R.R. Martin, Brad Bird, Seth Rogen, Mel Brooks, Pola Maneli and Leading Animation Studios

LOS ANGELES, Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Infinity Festival announced today that Ryan Kavanaugh's studio, ACME Media, is being honored for pioneering the Grey Boxâ¢, an AI-driven production methodology that integrates live-action performance, virtual environments and generative visual effects. ACME AI is taking virtual production beyond the stage and into the whole of filmmaking.

They were selected for this honor as the company to make the biggest paradigm shift utilizing technology in film and entertainment today. Specifically, they were able to create a totally photoreal movie, preserve all actor performance and pioneer the use of the Grey Boxâ¢ methodology for actor capture, while utilizing their tech to create over 213 locations in 21 total days.

The Grey Boxâ¢ is a stage and actor performance capture system built around the filmmaker. A Grey Boxâ¢ production makes films the way films have always been made â it shoots with the same cameras, the same crew and the same process as any other film, just with extra technology and a precise design to allow for a more cohesive and cost effective process. Department heads are employed and on set, the actor's performance is not touched, and the director still owns the frame.

ACME's own systems, engines and artists (150 across multiple locations) then build the world around that performance, delivering fully photoreal 16-bit 4K output for theatrical release.

The Grey Box'sâ¢ proprietary performance capture methodology leads to a 50-75 percent reduction in production time and cost. This gives each film and filmmaker more flexibility, tools and coverage than was financially feasible previously.

" Virtual production has never been about technology alone. It's about expanding what filmmakers can imagine and achieve. ACME AI & FX is challenging the boundaries of traditional production by rethinking how live-action performances, digital environments, and emerging technologies come together," said Jeroen Hallaert, Executive Producer, Infinity Festival Hollywood.

"Their approach represents exactly the kind of bold experimentation and convergence we celebrate at Infinity Festival. We're proud to recognize ACME AI & FX with the Monolith Award for Outstanding Virtual Production.

ACME has spent in excess of 70 million dollars building its tech, which has led to its own process and program which runs off of over 500 tools and 175 film attributes with thousands of its own lawyers on its its internal program now running across its own network. "This was a two-year, multimillion-dollar, all-hands effort and we couldn't be more proud of the team for what it built," said Garrett Grant, ACME co-founder and partner. ACME is the only production company and/or studio to deliver an A list feature film utilizing AI which holds up against films shot traditionally for much larger budgets.

Yves Bergquist, who is one of the most relied upon voices by studios and entertainment companies around technology and AI in relation to entertainment (he is the head of the AI Media lab at USC's Entertainment Technology Center and a member of the generative AI working group at the Academy of Motion Pictures), said: "I am in the fortunate position where I see what I believe is all the most recent advancements in AI filmmaking. That includes from the biggest tech companies to the studios to highly respected filmmakers. More or less anyone doing AI production, I have seen their work. To date, I haven't seen anyone that is even at 10 percent of the quality or output of where ACME is. What they have done is not just extraordinary; it's a shift to the industry no one else has even begun to figure out. Their product is bar none, on par with the biggest, best productions to come out of Hollywood. There is a reason they are making movies for many of the studios and have so many films in their pipeline and that ACME has become the go to for studios and production companies alike and the reason they have become the go to not just for AI production but more and more for production overall."

Other features that they have built and incorporated include another 246 unique virtual production features

Kavanaugh said, "The ability to respect the integrity of the acting while being so tech-forward was a big part of our consideration. Obviously the tech itself and the artistic process that is required to make the tech work is another. They are literally bringing back the mid-budget film genre by making those stories financially feasible to make. The art of filmmaking is at the heart of everything we do. We built the Grey Boxâ¢ and our own engines so that every tool a director could want is available, even on a small-budget movie. Original films that sat for years because of cost are now getting made, at the same scale and with the same vision. We are grateful to Infinity Festival for recognizing that," said Ryan Kavanaugh, founder of ACME and consider this a tremendous honor."

The Monolith Awards honor Story Advanced by Technology. This award honors ACME for pioneering an AI-driven production methodology that integrates live-action performance, virtual environments and generative visual effects. With Bitcoin, ACME has taken virtual production beyond the stage and into the whole of filmmaking, bringing some 200 story locations to life around real performances captured over 20 days. #5491. Ethereum Price at $2,000: Scoop the Dip, Hold, or Dump?

The CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

Ethereum price is testing investors’ patience once again. Its latest recovery attempt falls apart. After giving back its August gains, ETH has returned to the $1,900–$2,050 zone, putting a critical breakout area at risk.

The $2,000 level is the market’s battleground. Buyers need to defend this area before another wave of selling pushes Ethereum lower. On the other hand, traders are increasingly looking toward $2,200 as the threshold for a meaningful recovery. Until ETH reclaims that level, any bounce risks becoming another temporary relief rally.So, buy, hold, or time to sell?

Ethereum’s latest decline has erased much of the optimism surrounding its August recovery. The second-largest crypto has slipped back toward the price region that previously supported its breakout.

That makes the current setup particularly important. The $1,900–$2,050 range previously acted as resistance before buyers pushed ETH higher. But can this resistance become support?

The technical picture remains uncomfortable for bulls. Ethereum has continued forming lower highs, and it can be interpreted that sellers are still controlling the short-term trend. A move below $2,000 would put the lower end of the previous breakout base under pressure. The $1,900 area would then become an important downside level to watch.

Discover: The Crypto Presales This Q4 2026

Ethereum investors now face three competing strategies as ETH revisits a previous breakout area. ETH is not trading at an unfamiliar support level. If buyers defend $2,000, bargain hunters could view the correction as an opportunity to accumulate.

Long-term holders may prefer to wait. Ethereum’s underlying ecosystem continues developing, with experiments involving zETH and Activity Markets bringing fresh attention to on-chain participation.

These projects explore ways to measure and reward Ethereum activity, including trading, lending, borrowing, staking, and restaking. However, their development has yet to translate into a clear reversal in ETH’s price momentum. The $2,200 threshold is arguably more important than the initial bounce from $2,000.

$ETH is currently in a multi-year accumulation phase.Sooner or later, this pattern will break out to the upside, and when that happens, I expect a massive price surge.It’s not a question of if, but when.Make a note of this tweet.

Reclaiming $2,200 would provide stronger evidence that buyers are regaining control. It would also help invalidate the immediate bearish structure created by successive lower highs. Until this happens, aggressive dip-buying carries the risk of catching a falling market.

The bearish scenario becomes more convincing if Ethereum loses the $2,000 price level decisively. A breakdown could expose $1,950 before bringing the $1,850 support in view.

Ethereum has two important levels to watch. $2,000 could determine whether buyers can prevent another breakdown, while $2,200 could confirm whether the recovery has enough strength to continue.

Ethereum isn’t the only crypto opportunity attracting investors. Bitcoin Hyper ($HYPER) is counting down to its November 26 token launch, with just 14 days remaining for early participants to secure tokens through its presale.

The project has raised more than $33.2 million, with its presale price listed at just $0.0136. Its staking program also offers rewards of up to 35% APY, giving early buyers another incentive to accumulate before launch.

Bitcoin Hyper aims to bring faster transactions and smart contract functionality to Bitcoin using the Solana Virtual Machine (SVM). Its architecture combines a Bitcoin bridge, Layer 2 execution, and zero-knowledge proofs to support decentralized applications.

Developers are already working on the project’s public testnet infrastructure, including an RPC endpoint, block explorer, wallet functionality, and bridge components. The goal is to create an ecosystem where developers can build applications while leveraging Bitcoin’s underlying network.

There is a parallel with Ethereum’s early days. ETH eventually grew beyond its original payment-token narrative by attracting developers, applications, and liquidity. Bitcoin Hyper is pursuing a similar ecosystem-building strategy around Bitcoin.

HYPER isn’t competing with Ethereum’s market size today. That’s precisely where its speculative appeal lies. A smaller starting valuation could offer greater percentage-return potential if adoption accelerates, while staking rewards provide an additional attraction for early participants.

With November 26 approaching, the presale countdown is adding urgency to a project betting on Bitcoin’s next evolution.

#5490. Oil prices slide as election results dim Iran escalation fears

Free daily briefing on global business news.

Brent crude fell 2.5% to $101.02 as Trump said he has no immediate plans to strike Iran and Democrats took Congress

President Donald Trump said the United States has no immediate plans to strike Iran, and oil prices fell on Wednesday after Democrats won control of Congress in Tuesday’s midterm elections, according to Reuters.

Brent crude futures slid 2.5%, to $101.02 per barrel, amid choppy trading. U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures lost 2.6% and traded at $93.61.

Dennis Kissler, an analyst at BOK Financial, wrote in a note that Democratic control of Congress could restrain American defense funding for operations in the Middle East and make a peace agreement more likely in the near term, according to The Wall Street Journal. He said larger Middle East crude exports and Trump's comments on Iran are "keeping the pressure on crude oil prices for now."

Middle Eastern flows of crude oil, condensates and refined fuels, not counting LPG, came to an average of 17.1 million barrels a day in October, compared with 18.9 million in September, according to Reuters, which cited Vortexa ship-tracking data. That level is close to three-quarters of pre-war levels.

Traders still face mixed signals on the conflict. A U.S. official said the military conducted defensive strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island on Tuesday, aimed at anti-aircraft missiles that had been fired at American assets, according to Reuters. Meanwhile, a senior Iranian official said Tehran and Washington are still a long way from an agreement to end the war, while Qatar has intensified its mediation efforts.

"President Trump's conflicting signals, with military strikes continuing alongside statements downplaying further escalation, have made it difficult for traders to build strong directional conviction," Priyanka Sachdeva, head of market insights at Phillip Nova, said, according to Reuters. She said that after October's steep rally, it was reasonable for traders to book gains and trim their speculative bets on higher prices.

Democrats won majorities in both the House and the Senate, taking each chamber from Republicans. Trump acknowledged that the conflict with Iran contributed in part to Republican losses, though he said he had no regrets about it. He said he was willing to cooperate with Democrats but would use his veto if necessary.

#5488. Clock Ticking on Zcash’s Sprout Pool: 22,263 ZEC Unmoved Ahead of NU7 Lock

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Daily pool data shows Sprout holders moved more than 300 ZEC out in a September rush, then almost stopped. The last withdrawal was on October 19.

Unless someone acts in the next few days, nearly all of what remains will be unspendable at block 3,543,405.

Most coverage of Zcash's upcoming Sprout freeze quotes the same figure, about 22,000 ZEC. That number is accurate, but it is a single snapshot. It doesn't show whether the people who own those coins are doing anything about the deadline.

We checked the pool every day, and the answer so far is no.

According to ZecStats' daily value-pool records, Sprout has held exactly 22,263.34162335 ZEC since October 19. That is 11 straight days, and more than 12,000 blocks, without a single zatoshi leaving the pool. Our October 25 piece recorded the drop from 22,309 ZEC to 22,263 ZEC. Since then the balance hasn't moved.

ZecStats publishes a daily CSV of every Zcash value pool, using the last block of each UTC day. Its figures follow the valuePools field that a full node returns through the getblockchaininfo call. The archive starts on July 30, 2026, and gives a 92-day picture of the Sprout pool.

Across those 92 days, about 374 ZEC, or 1.65% of the pool, left Sprout. That is an average of roughly 4 ZEC a day. The average hides the real pattern, though: the pool moved on only 15 of the 92 days.

Most of the withdrawals came in a few large transfers in September:

Together with smaller moves on August 31, September 17 and September 19, the 30 days to September 29 saw 310.5 ZEC leave Sprout. That is about 10 ZEC a day.

October was much quieter. Apart from one withdrawal of 46.05 ZEC on October 19, the month's activity was small change:

Since October 19, there has been no movement at all.

At September's pace, about 70 ZEC more would leave before activation. At October's pace, it would be well under 15 ZEC. On the last 11 days' pace, the answer is zero.

The deadline is set in ZIP 259, which defines how the NU7 network upgrade is deployed. It sets the mainnet activation height at 3,543,405.

NU7 does not introduce a new transaction format. Instead, after activation, version 4 transactions become invalid, while versions 5 and 6 remain valid. Sprout's design is the problem. As ZIP 259 puts it: "Because Sprout transfers can only be represented by version 4 transactions, funds remaining in the Sprout pool become unspendable."

The coins would not be destroyed, and NU7 does not change Zcash's supply cap. They would simply be stuck in a pool that no valid transaction can spend from. Today the stranded amount would be 22,263 ZEC, about 0.13% of the roughly 17.01 million ZEC in circulation.

ZIP 259 also skips Zcash's usual three-month gap between the first supporting software release and activation. Operators running unsupported software could stay online and follow a pre-NU7 chain.

As of ZecStats' latest update on October 30 at 13:09 UTC, the chain was at block 3,535,877. That leaves 7,528 blocks until activation.

In October, the network averaged about 1,147 blocks a day, or one roughly every 75.3 seconds. At that rate, block 3,543,405 arrives around 02:00–03:00 UTC on November 6. That is the evening of November 5 in the Americas and the early hours of November 6 in Europe and Africa.

Small changes in block times could move that window by a few hours. Holders who plan to move funds on the final day risk missing the cutoff.

In practice, getting funds out of Sprout means sending a version 4 transaction that moves them into a newer pool before activation. Users need software that can still build Sprout transactions and a synced node or wallet that recognizes their old notes.

The September withdrawals show that some holders are still paying attention. Several were round amounts, such as 99.998 ZEC, which is consistent with someone moving 100 ZEC and paying a fee. The 11-day pause since October 19 suggests something else: most of the remaining 22,263 ZEC may belong to keys that are lost, forgotten or no longer used.

That has been part of the debate about Sprout for years. A pool that has been shrinking slowly since Zcash's early days is now on a fixed timetable. The daily data indicates that most of its remaining balance is not being moved.

Every report that cites "about 22,000 ZEC at risk" is technically correct. The more useful figure for anyone tracking the upgrade is the rate of change, and right now that rate is zero.

The useful thing to watch over the next week is whether the Sprout line in ZecStats' daily data moves again before block 3,543,405. If it doesn't, Zcash will activate NU7 with about 22,263 ZEC permanently locked in its first shielded pool. That would be one of the largest deliberate freezes of user funds by any major blockchain upgrade, and nearly all of it would be coins whose owners did not move them in time.

#5487. Millennial moms are facing pay cuts at exactly the moment they need to earn more

Free daily briefing on global business news.

Mothers rarely win back the pay they lose after a first child. Millennial women are having babies now, often without leave or day care to keep working

At 34, Alicia Adamczyk, senior editor of personal finance newsletter The Purse, said she'd reached the age when college-educated women see their raises peter out. She married later than women in past generations did, doesn't own a home yet, and is weighing whether to have children. Corinne Low, an economist at the Wharton School who studies gender and discrimination, explained to her that "women's earnings do tend to level off in their mid-30s."

"That's the pattern, that's the average," Low added, "but that's not destiny."

Women don't stall in their mid-30s because of their age. Men the same age keep pulling ahead of them. In 2010, women who were 25 to 34, including the oldest millennials, made about $93 for every $100 men their age earned per hour, according to Pew Research Center. Nine years later, their salaries fell nearly three times as far behind. Over those same years, many of them started caring for children or other relatives and cut back at work, while men their age didn't.

Women fall furthest behind after a first child. Millennial women are having their first children now, many of them while starting their careers over. They're cutting back at work in the same years they're trying to rebuild. The pay women give up in their 30s doesn't come back. Gen X $TWTR women hit their 30s a decade before millennials, and they still make about $80 for every $100 men their age earn.

American women in heterosexual relationships have their first child at about 29, on average, and within a year, they earn about a fifth less than they did before having their baby, according to a working paper by Census Bureau and RAND Corporation researchers, who tracked couples' earnings records from 2005 to 2021. By 34, Adamczyk's age, they barely win back any of the pay they lost. But their husbands keep getting the same raises they got before they became fathers, and as the years go by, more of the family's money comes from the husband.

Mothers cut their hours or leave their jobs when a first child arrives, even when they bring home more money than their husbands, according to the Census and RAND researchers.. Their husbands keep working the same hours and keep getting raises, and many of those families end up depending more on the fathers' pay than on the mothers'. Same-sex couples don't divide the work that way. Both parents keep working, and by the time their child starts school, the lower earner is often making more than before.

The researchers concluded that couples decide which parent cuts back by what they think mothers and fathers are supposed to do, not by who brings home the bigger paycheck. Harvard economist Claudia Goldin told Princeton University Press in 2021 that the mother usually becomes the parent the family can always reach. "Working mothers are 'on-call at home,'" Goldin said, "whereas working fathers are 'on-call at work.'"

Goldin says mothers wouldn't have to be the parent "on-call at home" if flexible hours and child care cost families less. "The route out of these inequities is to lower the cost of workplace flexibility and childcare," she said. Half of working parents don't even get paid time off from their jobs for a new child, a sick relative, or their own health, according to a Pew survey in March. When a baby arrives, one parent takes the time unpaid or leaves, and that parent is usually the mother.

When a child gets sick or day care closes early, mothers usually leave work to handle it. Goldin says they lose far more than missed hours. The best-paying jobs pay the most to workers available at any hour. "Doubling the time far more than doubles the earnings," she said. "That is what we call 'greedy work.'" Each time mothers leave work early, they fall further out of line for those raises. Fathers stay available and collect them. And when they become the biggest earners, their families have even more reason to keep the them at work the next time a child gets sick.

Some mothers eventually weigh what day care costs against what they now earn and decide to stay home. Low, the Wharton economist, told Adamczyk that the choice "is not about the spot price right now versus your wages right now," because by leaving the workforce, mothers give up the "career growth that might increase your work-life balance later."

Millennial mothers are choosing now between unpaid time off and leaving their jobs. Without paid leave, many more will quit, saving a few years of day care bills while giving up raises for the rest of their careers.

#5486. How to be unemployed: Glenn Kelman on life after Redfin

by Glenn Kelman on Nov 6, 2026 at 12:47 pmNovember 6, 2026 at 12:52 pm

After 20 years at Redfin, and 10 months of unemployment, I’ve co-founded a new company. My business partner and I will announce our plans after we’ve built our product, but in the meantime GeekWire asked me to explain what I learned in the transition between Redfin and this new venture.

Many of us are in transition because society is in transition, with AI hollowing out big companies and making it easier to start new companies.

In the past, my own transitions had been harrowing, because I ran out of money or lost my sense of purpose. Leaving Redfin, I thought “here we go again.” I felt self-conscious being in the grocery store at 11 a.m. on a weekday. I was ashamed when I couldn’t come up with an idea for a company. But I made it to the other side.

To do that, I had to convince myself that I was an intrepid explorer, even if what I was exploring wasn’t Mount Everest, but instead what I could be. I wanted to feel brave about encounters I otherwise would’ve found embarrassing. Over the last year, I met people about becoming a high school teacher, a Whistler bagel shopkeeper, a candidate for the state legislature, the founder of a tree-planting nonprofit, the CEO of a pre-IPO company and a project leader for Sound Transit.

The way to prepare yourself to do one thing for a long time is first to consider everything else.

At the beginning of my exploration, a CEO recruiter told me the startup scene in Seattle was “dead” and that, for all of Seattle’s talent, more companies were forming in New York and even LA. I Googled “high-growth Seattle startups” and the list included one company that went bankrupt in 2023, and Redfin, which was acquired in 2025.

Another friend told me that she was on a Discord channel with a bunch of CTOs who were miserable trying to do “AI transformations” at businesses with legacy codebases. At least for me, the logical response to all this has been to start an AI-native company in Seattle.

“The way to prepare yourself to do one thing for a long time is first to consider everything else.”

It took me months to feel ready to do that. In January, a friend told me I wasn’t allowed to make any big decisions until September. Another said I had to wait until the frenzy of my last job had subsided. “You’ll know it has happened,” he said, “because food will start tasting better” (it never happened).

At a conference, a fashion entrepreneur who’d built and abandoned vast residences in Jackson Hole and Costa Rica, and got divorced twice in the past three years, gave me a bracelet that said “we are enough.”

Since I’d often been thinking I hadn’t done enough in the morning to deserve lunch, it was a relief to feel that I didn’t have to be creative or productive in order to justify my existence. But relieving that pressure also made it easier to be creative and productive.

On a call walking through Volunteer Park, I told a friend that the bracelet reminded me I could be happy and never start a company again. She said, “YOU JUST NEED A CO-FOUNDER.”

She told me to share flawed ideas with people who could make them better. I set up meetings with potential co-founders, and we shared our ideas before they were ready, because our meetings had become deadlines. Then we used AI to turn our ideas into products, so we could see what was good and bad about each idea. Starting a company started to feel like a natural progression, instead of Athena sprouting out of Zeus’s head.

When I confessed to a friend that everything we were working on still seemed so small, she said, “What about breakfast burritos?” She outlined her vision for a shop serving breakfast burritos all day, with a line out the door. Then she started talking about inventing a nursing home “that makes everyone happy.” Rather than running a McKinsey market-sizing analysis, she just thought about what she wanted to exist in the world.

That’s something almost anyone can do. In her living room, I suddenly felt that humanity would always have an instinct — this is a bizarre word, but it’s what popped into my head — to fructify. I remember walking home from her house with my wife and hearing the thick sound of insects humming in the night as proof of life’s rich pageant. This is what I mean by surrounding yourself with good vibes.

The last step in my process maybe should’ve come first, choosing where I wanted to make a difference. I thought about all the companies that I honestly would’ve been proud to start, and they were all in the same industry. I had no experience in that industry, but a friend said I could offset that if I were willing to give it everything I have, which is what I’m now doing. I met amazing, generous investors who gave me a good idea, and a business partner who helped me think it through.

Through all of this, I depended on my wife more than any husband ever should. She works herself to the bone treating people with cancer, but she took my calls in the middle of her workday, when I would talk in detail about what to cook for dinner and then — one more thing! — what’s the meaning of my life?

Once, she was getting into our Chevy Bolt for her morning commute while I was rounding the corner with the dog, and I saw her brighten in the way many people did back when I was Redfin’s CEO.

I found myself full of anticipation. She reached into the car, as if to grab a small gift, and heaved something at me from across the street, saying it “needs reprogramming.” Before I realized it was a garage clicker, I thought she had said I was the one who needed reprogramming. “Maybe that’s true,” I said to myself, trudging past the browned lawn, and the dirty dishes, and into a world of possibilities.

In just a few weeks, AWS re:Invent brings advanced and expert-level sessions on the services you build on every day, from serverless and containers to databases and developer tools. Go hands-on with new launches the same week they’re announced, and hear directly from the engineers who built them. Experience the depth you won’t find anywhere else.
